title: When the Program Runs but Is Wrong
content:
What problem does this solve?
Many bugs do not crash — they produce the wrong result. Logical errors require a small, disciplined routine: state an expected result; run and record the actual result; trace the few values that control the wrong result; identify where the values first diverge; change one cause and rerun both the failing and a boundary case. print can be used temporarily as a tracer, but finished functions should return the requested result.

Previously in your program
You read tracebacks and fixed syntax/name/type/index/key failures. Now you will repair programs that run successfully but produce an incorrect value.
concepts: Logical errors do not crash — they produce the wrong output
Trace the values that drive the wrong result
Identify the first point of divergence and change one cause
Verify both the failing and a boundary case after a fix

examples.title: Check the tighter boundary first
examples.explanation: Test the more specific three-key boundary before the broader one-key boundary.

common_mistakes: Reordering elif branches so the general case blocks a specific case
Updating a loop variable before recording the current value
Using the wrong dictionary key in a nested record

exercises.title: Runs without crashing
exercises.prompt: A program finishes normally but labels an 80-point signal as "Ready" instead of "Elite". What kind of problem is this?
exercises.success_message: Correct — the program ran, but its logic produced the wrong result.
exercises.failure_message: Successful execution can still be wrong. Here the behavior is incorrect without a traceback.
hints: Syntax stops parsing before the program runs.
Runtime errors produce a traceback during execution.
Logic errors run and print the wrong result.

exercises.title: Trace the chosen branch
hints: Decisions use the value at the moment the branch runs.
At 40, health < 50 is true after the first test fails.
The later +10 does not change which branch already ran.

exercises.title: Put the specific branch first
exercises.prompt: Repair the branch order so a score of 80 is Elite.
hints: A more specific boundary (>= 80) must be tested before the general (>= 50).
Reorder the conditions; do not change the labels.
Leave the Hold case as the final default.

exercises.title: Remove the off-by-one result
exercises.prompt: Fix countdown so it returns [start, ..., 1] (no 0). Keep a while loop you can trace.
hints: Decide whether to append before or after the decrement.
Return values from start down to 1, not including 0.
Keep a real function-scoped while loop; do not switch to for.

tests.message: Use a while loop whose condition can become true and change inside countdown.
countdown(0) should return an empty list.

exercises.title: Repair the expedition report
exercises.prompt: Fix the accumulator and condition so total_health is the sum of every member's health, and needs_rest is True when any member has health below 5. Health exactly 5 does not require rest. Return exactly the three requested keys.
hints: Accumulate by adding each member's health to the running total.
needs_rest becomes True when any member's health is below 5.
Return member_count, total_health, and needs_rest only.

tests.message: Keep a for loop in expedition_report and compute totals there.
Empty party → count 0, total 0, rest False.
One member at 8 → count 1, total 8, rest False.
Sum every member's health and set needs_rest correctly.
At the boundary 5, rest is not required.
